faq.question: Is SkillTube only for AI skills?
faq.answer: Skills are our main focus, but you can also list MCP servers, AI-related datasets and databases, prompts, agents and AI tools.

faq.question: GitHub already lets me publish and search. Why SkillTube?
faq.answer: SkillTube adds structured cards, 39 tags, a developer channel, fair ranking, owner verification, and clean pages that people and AI crawlers can read fully.

faq.question: Can AI assistants and crawlers read SkillTube?
faq.answer: Yes. Public pages need no JavaScript, have Markdown twins, structured data, a sitemap and llms.txt. Source links are never placed on public pages.

faq.question: Do I have to move my repository?
faq.answer: No. Your repository stays on GitHub; SkillTube only lists it.

faq.question: What is SkillTube?
faq.answer: A free directory where developers list AI skills, MCP servers, datasets, databases, prompts, agents and other AI tools. Each listing links to a public GitHub repository.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. No payment, no subscription, no ads.

faq.question: Who runs it?
faq.answer: Let's Code India, an open-source organisation in India.

faq.question: Do you host my files?
faq.answer: No. Files stay in your GitHub repository.

faq.question: Which languages is the site in?
faq.answer: English for now.

faq.question: Who can sign up?
faq.answer: Anyone aged 18 or over with a GitHub account at least 3 months old.

faq.question: Why GitHub only?
faq.answer: It lets us verify that you own the repository you list.

faq.question: Can I use it without an account?
faq.answer: You can browse public pages and developer profiles. Opening Source, starring, following and publishing need a login.

faq.question: How do I delete my account?
faq.answer: Settings → Delete account. Your profile, skills, follows, stars and comments are removed immediately.

faq.question: Why was my account blocked or removed?
faq.answer: Under-age, repeated serious violations (3 badge-removal removals), or a legal order. Contact us on any of the three emails.

faq.question: How many skills can I publish?
faq.answer: You start with 25. More slots unlock with views, followers and invites.

faq.question: How long can names and descriptions be?
faq.answer: Name 15 characters, short description 150, long description 1500.

faq.question: What are the 39 tags?
faq.answer: You pick 3 topics from 15, then 9 and 27 more tags under them. All are required.

faq.question: Why can't I edit right now?
faq.answer: Edits are rate-limited (lock shown with days left).

faq.question: What image sizes are allowed?
faq.answer: 3 KB normally, 10 KB for Blue/Master Tick holders; SVG, and PNG where the rules allow.

faq.question: What happens if I delete my GitHub repo?
faq.answer: The listing is removed after two consecutive failed checks (about 12 hours).

faq.question: Can I list someone else's repo?
faq.answer: No. The repo owner must be the logged-in account.

faq.question: How do I report a listing?
faq.answer: Use Report on the skill or channel; pick a reason and add a note up to 150 characters.

faq.question: Does the developer see who reported?
faq.answer: No.

faq.question: How long does the developer have to reply?
faq.answer: A set window; one reminder is sent three days before it ends.

faq.question: What is hidden immediately?
faq.answer: Reports marked serious (malware, illegal, violence/terror) hide the listing at once.

faq.question: Copyright complaint?
faq.answer: Use the `takedown_request` issue template or email us.

faq.question: How do I earn a badge?
faq.answer: Each badge page shows "how to earn".

faq.question: What is the Blue Tick?
faq.answer: 1,000,000 followers. It means fame, not identity verification.

faq.question: What is the Master Tick?
faq.answer: 100 Blue-Tick followers from at least 10 countries.

faq.question: What are the weekly ranks?
faq.answer: The top 50 developers by weekly score in bands of ten; only the best band shows on your profile.

faq.question: Are badges removed?
faq.answer: Yes, if a skill that earned a badge is removed after a report.

faq.question: What do you store?
faq.answer: GitHub id, username, avatar URL, the country you choose, follows, stars, comments, reports, counters and badges.

faq.question: Do you store my IP?
faq.answer: Never.

faq.question: Do you use analytics or tracking cookies?
faq.answer: No.

faq.question: Is my country public?
faq.answer: Never.

faq.question: How long do you keep removal records?
faq.answer: 180 days.

faq.question: Who handles complaints?
faq.answer: Our Grievance Officer — see the Grievance page.

faq.question: Is the code open?
faq.answer: Yes, MIT.

faq.question: How do I report a security bug?
faq.answer: See the Security page and `.well-known/security.txt`.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Only a basic offline page.

faq.question: Is there an API?
faq.answer: Not public yet.

faq.question: Where can I see service status?
faq.answer: The Status page.

faq.question: Where is the documentation?
faq.answer: Read the SkillTube documentation for guides to publishing, limits, reports, privacy and AI-tool access.

posts.title: Why we built SkillTube
posts.summary: Useful AI resources are scattered across repositories; SkillTube adds one free, structured place to discover them.

posts.title: Finding a good AI skill is harder than writing one
posts.summary: Names, descriptions, tags and activity signals help people compare projects beyond repository names.

posts.title: Every listing lives in its own public GitHub repository
posts.summary: Ownership, history, licence and issues stay with the developer; SkillTube provides a discovery card and link.

posts.title: Free for developers and users, with no credit card
posts.summary: SkillTube is designed around open-source software and free service plans, with no paid APIs or subscriptions.

posts.title: Owners are checked against GitHub
posts.summary: GitHub sign-in and recurring repository checks help keep listings tied to their owners.

posts.title: Dead listings clean themselves up
posts.summary: The catalog job checks repositories repeatedly and removes listings after consecutive failed checks.

posts.title: AI needs data, not only skills
posts.summary: Datasets, vector stores and databases deserve the same clear discovery as prompts and agents.

posts.title: Small developers get a fair chance
posts.summary: A mixed-strength search approach is intended to give useful new listings a path to discovery.

posts.title: Badges and ticks you cannot buy
posts.summary: SkillTube awards badges through published activity rules; audience ticks are not paid verification.

posts.title: Reporting that is fair to both sides
posts.summary: Reports allow a developer response, preserve reporter privacy and hide serious listings while reviewed.

posts.title: We store as little as possible
posts.summary: SkillTube does not store IP addresses or run analytics; country stays private and minimal records expire.

posts.title: Why SkillTube is 18+
posts.summary: The service requires adult users and GitHub accounts that meet the age requirement.

posts.title: Open to the world
posts.summary: SkillTube is a free, open-source community layer from Let's Code India for developers everywhere.

posts.title: Open source, with the rules in public
posts.summary: MIT-licensed code, public docs and an error-code table make the project easier to inspect.

posts.title: Light, fast and works on a phone
posts.summary: Native web technologies and server-rendered public pages keep the experience straightforward on small devices.

posts.title: Start in five minutes
posts.summary: A short path from GitHub sign-in to a tagged listing and a shareable developer channel.

posts.title: GitHub already exists. Why SkillTube?
posts.summary: GitHub keeps the code; SkillTube adds structured discovery, comparison and developer channels.

posts.title: Be found by people and by AI assistants
posts.summary: Server-rendered pages, Markdown twins, structured data and sitemaps give crawlers complete descriptions.

posts.title: Not only skills: MCP servers, datasets, databases and AI tools
posts.summary: Any AI-related resource in a public repository can use the same structured listing fields and tags.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.summary: Sign in with GitHub to publish and manage AI resources on SkillTube. AI skills are the main focus; MCP servers, datasets, databases, prompts, agents, AI tools and guides are welcome too.

docs.title: Limits and rules
docs.summary: SkillTube uses activity limits and cooldowns to keep publishing and community actions manageable. The app shows an error when an action is unavailable.

docs.title: Reporting content
docs.summary: Report a listing or developer channel when you believe it breaks the community rules. Reports are reviewed, and a report is not by itself proof that a claim is true.

docs.title: Responding to reports
docs.summary: If someone reports your listing or channel, SkillTube gives you a private notice and a response window. You can see what was reported, but never who submitted the report.

docs.title: Removals and appeals
docs.summary: This guide explains what happens when a listing or account is removed and how to ask the team to review a decision.

docs.title: Contacting us
docs.summary: Contact Let's Code India for account support, grievances, copyright notices or other questions about SkillTube.

docs.title: Announcements and updates
docs.summary: Announcements share news from the SkillTube team. Updates help you follow new activity from developers you follow.

docs.title: Badges and ranking
docs.summary: Badges and ticks are automatic activity signals displayed on SkillTube. They are not identity verification, and they appear only on SkillTube.

docs.title: Privacy and data
docs.summary: SkillTube stores account and activity information needed to run the service. Some profile and listing information is public; private account details are not.

docs.title: For AI tools
docs.summary: SkillTube publishes readable public pages for people, assistants and crawlers. AI skills are the main focus; the directory also covers MCP servers, datasets, databases, prompts, agents, AI tools and guides.
